questions.question: Hydroplaning usually happens:

options.text: When tires have the correct air pressure.
When driving slower than 15 mph.
Where water pools on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water pools on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water has collected on the road. Your car can hydroplane at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water. Hydroplaning is more likely if your tires do not have enough air or if the tread is worn down.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off the turn signal?

options.text: Before you start the turn
While you are turning
After you finish the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: After you finish the turn
questions.explanation: Keep your turn signal on the whole time you are turning. Turn it off only after you finish the turn.

questions.question: When going down a hill, your vehicle will:

options.text: Slow down.
Move at the same speed as on flat ground.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster when you go downhill. Slow down before you reach a downhill section.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess how heavy the load is on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a full check of your vehicle. You need to explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as fast as possible, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: You will be asked to change lanes during the driving test. Check traffic first and use the proper signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts might mean:

options.text: It rained recently.
The nuts might be loose.
The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts might be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean the nuts are loose. Check if the nuts are tight if you see rust.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a problem since it is stopped.
Is only a problem if you see passengers getting off.
Is always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful around a stopped bus. Passengers might be nearby. The bus might block your view or their view of you.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, the hoses should be:

options.text: Checked for leaks.
Firmly connected to the battery.
Carrying fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Count on your taillights to warn other drivers.
Not think about other drivers.
Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the roadside, turn on your four-way flashers. This is especially important when visibility is low. Put out warning devices within 10 minutes.

questions.question: Banked curves:

options.text: Have a safe speed posted.
Can be driven at any speed.
Should be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a safe speed posted.
questions.explanation: Banked curves have posted safe speeds. These speeds are safe for cars but may not be safe for larger vehicles like buses and trucks.

questions.question: People working on a broken-down vehicle on the side of the road:

options.text: Are probably aware of the traffic around them.
May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a broken-down vehicle. They may be focused on the repair and not paying attention to traffic around them.

questions.question: When putting out an electrical fire, you should:

options.text: Use water.
Use a B:C extinguisher.
Use an X extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a B:C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing and blinking a lot
Yawning a lot or rubbing your eyes
Staying in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, blinking a lot, or heavy eyelids; yawning a lot or rubbing your eyes; daydreaming; wandering thoughts; trouble remembering the last few miles; missing exits or signs; trouble keeping your head up; drifting from your lane; following too close; hitting shoulder rumble strips; or feeling restless and irritable.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually very alert.
Is usually more careful than a normal driver.
May take longer to make quick decisions than a normal driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: May take longer to make quick decisions than a normal driver.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers see and react to hazards slower than drivers who are not tired. Drowsy drivers cannot make quick decisions as well as other drivers.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out, you should:

options.text: Use a fire extinguisher.
Try to spray water on the flames.
Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away from the fire and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you do not know how to put out a fire, do not try to do it yourself. Move away and wait for firefighters to arrive. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: After picking up passengers, a driver should:

options.text: Let passengers sit down or get steady before starting to drive.
Honk the horn and pull back into traffic.
Start driving as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let passengers sit down or get steady before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Start and stop smoothly to keep passengers safe. After passengers board, give them time to sit down or hold on before you start driving.

questions.question: If you do not know how to put out a fire in your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Use water.
Stay in the vehicle.
Wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you do not know what type of extinguisher to use for a vehicle fire, especially a hazardous materials fire, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them put it out.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move into the left lane.
Drive faster.
Leave more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave more space between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, leave more space between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more room to move without sudden stops and gives the tailgater room to pass. Driving faster is not safe because the tailgater may just follow you closely at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle (CMV) should:

options.text: Only have a fire extinguisher if it carries hazardous materials.
Only have a fire extinguisher if it travels through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is charged and ready to use.

questions.question: If a truck has one, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Add fuel to the truck.
Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
Check the engine oil level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops a tractor-trailer from rolling backward when it is being started from a stop.
